name: Arithmetic with integers & decimals
description: Adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing with integers and decimals.

questions.explanation: Start at 3 and move 8 places left on a number line: 2, 1, 0, −1, … to −5. Taking 8 from 3 gives a negative answer. Swapping the numbers round gives 8 − 3 = 5, which is a different calculation.
Subtracting −3 moves 3 places to the right, the same as adding 3, so 4 − (−3) = 7. Treating the two minus signs as an ordinary subtraction gives 1. The answer is positive, not −7 or −1.

3 × 2 = 6, and both numbers have one decimal place, so the answer has two: 0.06. Adding the digits instead of multiplying gives 0.3 + 0.2 = 0.5. Writing 0.6 moves the point one place too few, and 0.006 one place too many.

questions.prompt: Priya works out 0.4 × 0.5 and writes 2.0. What has she done?

options.text: Put the decimal point in the wrong place

questions.explanation: 4 × 5 = 20, and there are two decimal places altogether, so 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.20 = 0.2. Priya has found 20 and kept it as 2.0, losing the two decimal places. Adding would give 0.9, and dividing would give 0.8.

questions.prompt: Amir works out 3 + 2² and gets 25, saying "3 + 2 = 5, then 5² = 25". What has he done?

options.text: Done the addition before the index
Squared the 3 as well as the 2

questions.explanation: The index applies only to the 2, so 3 + 2² = 3 + 4 = 7. Amir has added first and then squared the whole of 3 + 2. Multiplying 3 by 2² gives 12, and squaring the 3 gives 3² + 2 = 11.
Multiplication is done before addition: 6 × 4 = 24, then 15 + 24 = 39. Working left to right gives (15 + 6) × 4 = 84. Adding 15 + 6 × 4 as 15 + 6 = 21 then × 4 is the same error.

questions.prompt: Tick the calculations with a negative answer.
questions.explanation: −3 × 4 = −12, −3 − 4 = −7 and 4 − 10 = −6, all negative. −3 + 4 = 1, which is positive: there is more positive than negative. (−3) × (−4) = 12, because a negative times a negative is positive.

questions.prompt: Which calculation gives an answer less than 6?
questions.explanation: 6 × 0.5 = 3, which is less than 6. 6 ÷ 0.5 = 12 and 6 ÷ 0.2 = 30 are both bigger, because dividing by a number less than one asks how many of them fit. Multiplication does not always make a number bigger.
A negative times a negative is positive, so −3 × −4 = 12. The two minus signs do not both survive: −12 keeps one of them. Adding the numbers instead gives −3 + −4 = −7.
6 ÷ 0.5 asks how many halves are in 6, which is 12. 6 × 0.5 halves the 6 to 3, and adding or subtracting 0.5 moves it only a little. Multiplication does not always make a number bigger.

questions.prompt: At 6 am the temperature was −4 °C. By noon it had risen 9 °C. By 9 pm it had fallen 6 °C. What was the temperature at 9 pm?
questions.explanation: −4 + 9 = 5, so it was 5 °C at noon. Then 5 − 6 = −1, so it was −1 °C at 9 pm. Adding 9 and 6 and ignoring the sign gives 11, and dropping the minus at the end gives 1.

questions.prompt: A plank is 5.7 m long. A second plank is 0.4 m longer. How long is the second plank?
questions.explanation: Line up the decimal points: 5.7 + 0.4 means 5.7 + 0.4 = 6.1. Adding the digits after the point as 7 + 4 = 11 gives 5.11, which treats tenths as if they were ones. 6.11 carries the 1 as a whole as well, and 5.1 forgets it entirely.
4 + 6 = 10, 15 − 5 = 10, 2 × 5 = 10 and 20 ÷ 2 = 10. 12 − 3 = 9, so it does not give 10 — check what each operation does, not just which numbers are used.

questions.prompt: Does dividing always make a number smaller?
questions.explanation: Sometimes. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 is smaller than 6, but 6 ÷ 0.5 = 12 is bigger, because dividing by a number less than one asks how many of them fit. Dividing by 1 leaves it the same.

questions.prompt: Which calculation does not give a positive answer?
questions.explanation: −3 × 4 = −12, which is negative. −3 × −4 = 12 and 4 − (−3) = 7 are both positive, and so is 4 + 3 = 7. A negative times a positive is negative; a negative times a negative is positive.
